body.en: Atoms emit light only at certain wavelengths, giving a *line spectrum*. For hydrogen the lines fit the Rydberg equation. The Lyman series ($n_1$ = 1) is in the UV, the Balmer series ($n_1$ = 2) in the visible, and the Paschen ($n_1$ = 3), Brackett ($n_1$ = 4) and Pfund ($n_1$ = 5) series in the infrared.
body.kn: ಪರಮಾಣುಗಳು ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ತರಂಗಾಂತರಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತ್ರ ಬೆಳಕು ಹೊರಸೂಸುತ್ತವೆ—ರೇಖಾ ರೋಹಿತ. ಲೈಮನ್ ಸರಣಿ UVಯಲ್ಲಿ, ಬಾಮರ್ ಸರಣಿ ಗೋಚರ ಭಾಗದಲ್ಲಿ, ಪಾಶನ್, ಬ್ರಾಕೆಟ್, ಫಂಡ್ ಸರಣಿಗಳು IRನಲ್ಲಿ.

title.en: Bohr's energy levels and spectral series

say.en: In Bohr's model the electron can have only certain energies. The levels crowd together as n increases and reach zero at n equals infinity.
Jumps down to n equals 1 give the Lyman series in the ultraviolet; jumps down to n equals 2 give the Balmer series, which we see as visible lines.
The energy of level n is minus 2.18 times 10 to the minus 18, times Z squared over n squared, joules. The emitted photon carries the energy difference.
Example: the first Balmer line, n equals 3 to 2. The wavenumber is 15 233 per centimetre, so the wavelength is about 656 nanometres, the red H-alpha line.
Bohr's energy levels and spectral series.

body.en: Bohr proposed that the electron moves in fixed circular orbits (stationary states) without radiating energy. Its angular momentum is quantised, $m_e vr = nh/2\pi$. Energy is absorbed or emitted only when it jumps between orbits: ΔE = hν. For a hydrogen-like species, $E_n$ = −2.18 × 10$^{-18}$ (Z$^2$/n$^2$) J and $r_n$ = 52.9 (n$^2$/Z) pm. The *model* fails for multi-electron atoms and cannot explain the Zeeman and Stark effects.
body.kn: ಬೋರ್ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ನಿಶ್ಚಿತ ಕಕ್ಷೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಕಳೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳದೆ ಸುತ್ತುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಂದು ಕಕ್ಷೆಯಿಂದ ಇನ್ನೊಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಜಿಗಿದಾಗ ಮಾತ್ರ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಹೀರುತ್ತದೆ ಅಥವಾ ಹೊರಸೂಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಈ ಮಾದರಿ ಬಹು-ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಪರಮಾಣುಗಳಿಗೆ ವಿಫಲ.

heading.en: Bohr's Model, Hydrogen Spectrum, de Broglie and Heisenberg

tagline.en: Bohr's postulates, radii and energies of hydrogen-like orbits, the spectral series of hydrogen and the Rydberg equation, limitations of Bohr's model, the de Broglie wavelength and Heisenberg's uncertainty principle.

myth.en: Heisenberg's principle means our instruments are not good enough yet; better instruments will fix the electron's exact orbit.

truth.en: The uncertainty is built into nature. Any measurement of an electron's position (using light) disturbs its momentum, so Δx·Δp ≥ h/4π for every possible experiment. For everyday objects the limit is far below what we can measure, so it never shows. For an electron the uncertainty in velocity is as large as the velocity itself, so definite Bohr orbits cannot exist.

say.en: Bohr: stationary orbits, ΔE = hν, mvr = nh/2π.
rₙ = 52.9 n²/Z pm; Eₙ = −2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ Z²/n² J; vₙ = 2.18 × 10⁶ Z/n m s⁻¹.
Lyman (UV, n₁ = 1), Balmer (visible, n₁ = 2), Paschen, Brackett, Pfund (IR).
Bohr fails for many-electron atoms, fine structure, Zeeman and Stark effects.
λ = h/mv; Δx·Δp ≥ h/4π: exact orbits are impossible for electrons.

For everyday objects the limit is far below what we can measure, so it never shows. For an electron the uncertainty in velocity is as large as the velocity itself, so definite Bohr orbits cannot exist.

problem.en: An electron in a hydrogen atom falls from n = 5 to n = 2. Find the energy and wavelength of the light emitted.

steps.en: λ = 434 nm, a violet-blue line of the Balmer series.

say.en: Let us solve this together. An electron in a hydrogen atom falls from n equals 5 to n equals 2. Find the energy and wavelength of the light emitted.
delta E equals 2.18 times 10 to the power minus 18 (1 over 2 squared minus 1 over 5 squared) equals 2.18 times 10 to the power minus 18 times 0.21 equals 4.58 times 10 to the power minus 19 joules.
lambda equals hc over delta E equals (6.626 times 10 to the power minus 34 times 3.0 times 10 to the power 8)/(4.58 times 10 to the power minus 19) equals 4.34 times 10 to the power minus 7 metres.
lambda equals 434 nanometres, a violet-blue line of the Balmer series.
So the answer is 4.58 times 10 to the power minus 19 joules; 434 nanometres.

body.en: When electrons in many atoms fall from level n to the ground state, the maximum number of different lines is n(n − 1)/2. From n = 4: 4 × 3/2 = 6 lines. Between any two levels n₂ and n₁: (n₂ − n₁)(n₂ − n₁ + 1)/2.

say.en: Counting spectral lines. When electrons in many atoms fall from level n to the ground state, the maximum number of different lines is nn minus 1/2. From n equals 4: 4 times 3 over 2 equals 6 lines. Between any two levels n 2 and n 1: (n 2 - n 1)(n 2 - n 1 plus 1)/2.

homework.en: Calculate the ionisation energy of a hydrogen atom in J and in kJ mol⁻¹.

narration.en: Recap. Lyman (n₁ = 1) is UV, Balmer (n₁ = 2) is visible, the rest are IR. Bohr: fixed orbits, mvr = nh/2π, light only when the electron jumps. Eₙ = −2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ Z²/n² J and rₙ = 52.9 n²/Z pm. Bohr’s model works only for one-electron species.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಲೈಮನ್ (n₁ = 1) UV, ಬಾಮರ್ (n₁ = 2) ಗೋಚರ, ಉಳಿದವು IR. ಬೋರ್: ನಿಶ್ಚಿತ ಕಕ್ಷೆಗಳು, mvr = nh/2π, ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಜಿಗಿದಾಗ ಮಾತ್ರ ಬೆಳಕು. Eₙ = −2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ Z²/n² J ಮತ್ತು rₙ = 52.9 n²/Z pm. ಬೋರ್ ಮಾದರಿ ಏಕ-ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಪ್ರಭೇದಗಳಿಗೆ ಮಾತ್ರ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. Lyman n 1 equals 1 is UV, Balmer n 1 equals 2 is visible, the rest are IR.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ಲೈಮನ್ n 1 equals 1 UV, ಬಾಮರ್ n 1 equals 2 ಗೋಚರ, ಉಳಿದವು IR.

say.en: Bohr: fixed orbits, mvr equals nh over 2 pi, light only when the electron jumps.
say.kn: ಬೋರ್: ನಿಶ್ಚಿತ ಕಕ್ಷೆಗಳು, mvr equals nh over 2 pi, ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಜಿಗಿದಾಗ ಮಾತ್ರ ಬೆಳಕು.

say.en: E n equals minus 2.18 times 10 to the power minus 18 Z squared/n squared J and r n equals 52.9 n squared/Z pm.
say.kn: E n equals minus 2.18 times 10 to the power minus 18 Z squared/n squared J ಮತ್ತು r n equals 52.9 n squared/Z pm.

say.en: Bohr's model works only for one-electron species.
say.kn: ಬೋರ್ ಮಾದರಿ ಏಕ-ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಪ್ರಭೇದಗಳಿಗೆ ಮಾತ್ರ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.
